text:
Vince Dunn plays 22:51 a night for Seattle, and too many of those minutes are spent in his own end. At five-on-five the Kraken get only 40% of the shot attempts and 43% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and they're a bit worse with him than without.

Context matters. Evolving-Hockey found last season that he plays with some of the weakest teammates in the league (bottom 4% by their impact), which drags his raw on-ice numbers down. His own offense is steady: 11 points in 20 games, five on the power play, right in line with our range for him.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows both sides. He gets to the front of the net more than almost any defenseman (96th percentile for chances from the home-plate area), but only 31% of his exits keep possession, so watch for clears off the glass and icings when the forecheck comes. He's 30 and won a Stanley Cup with St. Louis in 2019. His last ten games have been quieter: four points, and about a minute less ice time a night.
headline: Vince Dunn is carrying a heavy load in Seattle
